biggest_catch: The 30% federal Residential Clean Energy Credit (IRC Section 25D) no longer exists for new purchases. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 4, 2025) terminated it for ALL expenditures made after December 31, 2025 — with no phase-down and no grace period. Only solar equipment whose installation was fully completed by 12/31/2025 qualifies (IRS FAQ, Aug 21, 2025: an expenditure 'is treated as made when the original installation of the item is completed'). A homeowner-owned system installed in 2026 gets 0% federal credit. The only surviving federal solar credit is the commercial Section 48E credit (available through 12/31/2027 for most projects), which goes to the leasing company — not the homeowner — under leases/PPAs, typically as lower monthly payments. The catalog's 'Install solar, claim tax credit on federal tax return — 30%' is stale; acting on it means expecting ~30% back (thousands of dollars) and getting nothing on a 2026 purchase.
catches: OBBBA Sec. 70506 rewrote 25D(h): the credit 'shall not apply with respect to any expenditures made after December 31, 2025' — per the CRS report IN12611, even a 2025 deposit with 2026 completion fails the test because the expenditure is 'made' when installation completes.
The credit was also nonrefundable when it existed: it could only offset tax owed (unused amounts could be carried forward), never produce a refund beyond liability.
Leased panels and PPAs were never eligible for 25D (owner-only credit); the surviving path is the lessor's commercial 48E credit, which is a different product with no homeowner tax filing.
The companion 25C Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit (30% up to $1,200/$2,000/yr) died on the same date — do not stack them in 2026 math.

State and utility solar incentives still exist (45 states + DC have some solar incentive per DSIRE's April 2026 summary) — they are separate, state-specific, and must be verified on DSIRE; they are not a federal 30%.

The IRS's own Residential Clean Energy Credit page now reflects the termination; third-party articles still quoting '30% through 2032' are outdated — verify against irs.gov or the CRS summary, not installer marketing.

c1.evidence: The IRS and U.S. Congress are real; irs.gov is the catalog's listed URL. The organization is real, so c1 passes honestly.

c2.evidence: FAIL: no current official terms support the claimed '30% of solar installation cost' for a 2026 purchase. CRS product IN12611 (congress.gov): 'P.L. 119-21 terminates the RCEC at the end of 2025.' IRS FAQ (Aug 21): installation completed after 12/31/2025 'will prevent the taxpayer from claiming the section 25D credit.'

c3.evidence: Claiming the credit when it existed required no fee (Form 5695 with the tax return); the 2026 failure is the terminated credit, not a fee. c3 passes honestly.

c4.evidence: FAIL: no official source quotes a 30% payout for 2026 homeowner installs. Current guides (updated Sept 2026) state flatly: '2026 and later homeowner-owned systems: 0 percent federal credit.'

eligibility: No current eligibility for the claimed 30% credit on new 2026 homeowner purchases. Legacy eligibility: owned systems with original installation completed by 12/31/2025 could still claim 30% on the 2025 return. Leased/PPA systems: homeowner never claimed 25D; lessor may use commercial 48E.
notes: Researched 2026-09-23. Verdict is REJECT: the catalog's claimed figure is definitively stale — the 30% rate and its entire phase-down schedule were wiped out by the July 2025 law. This is the highest-stakes reject in the batch because the dollar amounts are large (30% of a $20k-$40k install). Recommendation: retire R0317 or rewrite it as a 'check state/utility solar incentives on DSIRE' route with no federal-credit claim (that function overlaps R0322). app_links null — nothing verified.

s1.note: No eligible 2026 homeowner population for the claimed credit — terminated. Leased systems were never eligible for 25D.

s2.note: No fee to claim a credit, but installation costs $20k-$40k and the expected 30% offset no longer exists — the economics of the route have inverted.

s3.note: No payout timing exists for a terminated credit; the catalog's 'when filing taxes' has no current official source.

s4.note: '30% of solar installation cost' is now misinformation for 2026 installs — many installer sites and old articles still quote it. The official position is 0%.

s5.note: IRS direct page could not be fetched by the research tool; termination evidence comes from the authoritative CRS summary (congress.gov IN12611), the IRS FAQ of Aug 21, 2025 quoted in it, and 2026 guides updated within days of research.

s6.note: No steps can produce the claimed 30% credit on a 2026 purchase — steps array left empty per reject rules.

s7.note: Termination verified against CRS IN12611, IRS FAQ (Aug 2025), and multiple 2026-dated guides 2026-09-23; commercial 48E survival confirmed as the lessor-only path.

timing: No current federal payout — the credit is terminated for expenditures after 12/31/2025.

weasel_words.quote: '30% of solar installation cost' — the Section 25D credit at that rate was terminated for expenditures made after December 31, 2025; quoting 30% for 2026 installs is stale and cannot be delivered.
